info.bio:
Helmet es una banda de Metal Alternativo formada en 1989 por Page Hamilton como vocalista y primera guitarra, John Stanier en la batería, el australiano Peter Mengede en la guitarra rítmica y Henry Bogdan en el bajo.

Los 90 

El grupo debutó con Strap It On en 1990 con el sello Amphetamine Reptile, lo producen ellos mismos, y el resultado: riffs repetitivos, voces rabiosas y melodicas a la vez y el manejo de los tiempos es lo que identifica a Helmet como una banda única e inclasificable estilo.

scenes.name: Grunge
scenes.author: Piero Scaruffi
scenes.desc: El grunge, revival del hard rock de los setenta y renacimiento musical de Seattle, fue uno de los grandes fenómenos de los noventa (casi solo en EE UU). Green River lo inauguran (Come On Down) y Pearl Jam, Soundgarden, Melvins y Mudhoney fijan sus cuatro puntos cardinales; Nirvana, con Nevermind, lo convierten en una tragaperras y en la banda sonora de la crisis nerviosa de una generación. Después, Alice In Chains (Dirt), Foo Fighters, Hammerbox, GodHeadSilo, Everclear, Stone Temple Pilots, Tool (el grupo más innovador de la segunda generación: Aenima, Lateralus), God Machine, Helmet, Quicksand, Urge Overkill, los Smashing Pumpkins (Siamese Dream, Mellon Collie), Scarce, Creed, Bush, Manic Street Preachers, Silverchair.

concerts.title: Judgment Night (1993) Soundtrack Collaboration
concerts.body: Helmets went into the studio with House of Pain for the soundtrack of the 1993 movie "Judgment Night," resulting in a "big alternative club hit." "Helmets went into the studio with House of Pain."

xref.title: Arthur Brown (1968) – First Rock Star to Use Extreme Stage Makeup; Flaming Helmet; Set Stage for What Followed
xref.body: Arthur Brown of the Crazy World of Arthur Brown appears to have been the first rock star to use extreme makeup on stage, making it difficult to know what he really looked like. He also wore a helmet on stage which was often set on fire. Brown was born in Yorkshire, went to university in London and Reading, worked in theater, and was in several bands before this project. He was not exactly anonymous, but set the stage for the theatrical identity concealment that would follow. "Arthur Brown appears to have been the first rock star to use extreme makeup on stage, making it tough to know what he really looked like."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Origin of Daft Punk's Helmets – 1974 Brian De Palma Film Phantom of the Paradise; Sampler Explosion Fiction September 9, 1999
xref.body: After their rock band Darlin' dissolved in 1992 (following a Melody Maker review calling them "daft punky trash"), Thomas Bangalter and Guy-Manuel de Homem-Christo shifted to synths, drum machines, and sequencers. One of them saw the 1974 Brian De Palma film Phantom of the Paradise, whose disfigured main character Winslow Leech wore a helmet to hide his injuries — and Daft Punk adopted the helmet idea. The fictional mythology was that at 9:09am on September 9, 1999, a sampler exploded in their studio, horribly injuring both men and requiring helmets to be permanently installed; they had also become robots, losing all human memories but retaining the ability to create music. The helmets had built-in air conditioning (handy for hot live shows) and communication links. One set was made by the same special effects company that worked on one of the Spider-Man movies. Thomas and Guy-Manuel could walk through crowds at their own shows unrecognized. "For us, it was sci-fi glam. We're not performers, we're not models. It would not be enjoyable for humanity to see our features, but the robots are exciting to people."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: The Robot Helmets – 1974 Phantom of the Paradise; Air Conditioning; Communication Links; Spider-Man Effects Company
xref.body: The robot mythology was inspired partly by the 1974 Brian De Palma film Phantom of the Paradise, in which disfigured character Winslow Leech wore a helmet to hide his injuries, and partly by a 1970s band called Space, whose members wore helmets and spacesuits for anonymity. The first helmets had wigs (Thomas had curly hair, Guy-Manuel had long straight hair) until on the way to a 2001 magazine photo shoot they decided robots should look bald and ripped out the fake hair. The helmet designs became increasingly ornate: some reportedly had built-in air conditioning and communication links so they could talk to each other and their crew during performances. One set of helmets was made by the same special effects company that worked on one of the Spider-Man movies. The anonymity was so effective they could walk right through crowds at their own shows unrecognized. One impostor ran up a huge bar tab at a club in Ibiza by claiming to be Thomas Bangalter. "People thought the helmets were marketing or something, but for us, it was sci-fi glam."

xref.title: Supergroup Lineup and Origins (1994-2001)
xref.body: Tapeworm was conceived as a side project during Nine Inch Nails' "The Downward Spiral" sessions in 1994, intended as a collaborative effort for Danny Lohner and Charlie Clouser. It evolved to include a star-studded lineup: Trent Reznor, Maynard James Keenan (Tool), producer Alan Molder, Atticus Ross, Phil Anselmo and Rex Brown (Pantera), Page Hamilton (Helmet), Toni Halliday (Curve), Tommy Victor (Ministry), and drummer Josh Freese, with at least an album's worth of material recorded by 2001. "If you're Trent Rezner, Danny Loaner and Charlie Closer from his live band, Maynard James Keenan from Tool, producer Alan Molder and Atticus Ross. I mean, wow, awesome, right? The idea for tapeworm went as far back as the sessions for the downward spiral in 1994. Tapeworm was designed as something to which Danny and Charlie could contribute as equals. This idea evolved into something pretty cool. Maynard was brought in, Phil and Salmo from Pantera, Paige Hamilton from Helmut, Tony Haliday from a cool band called Curve, Tommy Victor from Ministry, drummer Josh Freeze. And then in 2001, Alan Molder apparently helped record at least an album's worth of stuff."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Project History (1995-2004)
xref.body: This project was created in 1995 and involved Trent Reznor, Atticus Ross, and a variety of friends, continuing off and on for nine years. Despite the collaboration, nothing was ever officially released. "I already mentioned the tapeworm project, which was created in 1995 and included a lot of different friends. They were continued off and on for nine years, but nothing was ever released."

xref.title: The Edgefest Panda Incident (1999)
xref.body: During the Matthew Good Band's performance on the main stage at Edgefest in Wilson Park, Barrie, in 1999, Universal Music marketing representative Iber Hamilton, dressed in a giant panda costume, attempted a stage dive during the song "Everything's Automatic." From the 10-12 foot high stage, he launched into the crowd, which unexpectedly parted "like the Red Sea." The panda landed face down on the ground 12 feet below, suffering a bleeding nose (his head was protected by a football helmet within the costume) and was subsequently kicked by some members of the audience. Matthew Good, performing with his microphone back by the monitor lines, did not immediately see what happened but later found Hamilton in the back with a bloody face. This incident later inspired the artwork for the "Loser Anthem" EP. "The crowd parts like the Red Sea. Everybody moves. Panda, bam! Face down on the ground, 12 feet below the stage."

xref.title: Early Career and Persona
xref.body: Susan Dietrich, known as The Space Lady, is from Pueblo, Colorado. For many years, she was a street musician, frequently performing in cities like Boston and San Francisco. She was easily recognizable by her unique outfit: a silver plastic helmet adorned with white wings and a flashing light. She initially played the accordion. "She wore a silver plastic helmet adorned with white wings and a flashing light on top. And she played the accordion."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Elaborate Helmet Designs
xref.body: Each iteration of their helmets became more elaborate, incorporating features like LED effects and internal air-conditioning units for hot performances. They also sometimes added leather outfits and capes to their attire. "Each iteration of the helmets became more elaborate. Some had LED effects built in while others had their own air-conducing units for those really hot cakes. Leather outfits were sometimes added. They brought in capes too."
